_supersedes: norris-r2-v1.json (48 trials, 2 conditions, k=8). Superseded because that design had three defects: three wordings per condition makes the wording-level test powerless by construction (minimum attainable p = 1/20), a single relative tolerance could not judge six significant digits, and two conditions cannot separate 'names R' from 'looks like software'.
_what: Everything that must be decided before the batch runs. Commit this file, then run. If any of it changes, plan_id changes and the change is visible in history.
_plan_id_note: sha of (arm table + prompt + schema + 'rep-major'). Reproduce with: python tools/batch_plan.py --task norris-ols --k 6 --family r-eco,py-eco,software,plain

design.order: rep-major: six rounds of 48, one of every wording per round
design.token_matching: all 48 wordings cost exactly 11 path tokens

execution._why_chunked: 288 trials in one go is one long opportunity to fail silently. Each chunk is a complete balanced replicate of the design -- all four conditions, all 48 wordings -- so a chunk that finishes is a usable experiment, and a chunk that goes wrong can be discarded without biasing anything.

concurrency._why: Wall clock only. A trial's start is registered when the call is made, so firing in planned order keeps startedAt ordered; measured Spearman(startedAt, planned order) = +1.000 with zero drift over the first 16 trials. Position is therefore preserved exactly, not approximated.
concurrency._why_not_trials_parameter: harness_run takes `trials: N`, but the workspace is fixed per CALL and reused by every trial inside it, and the trial loop awaits serially. Using it would put six runs in one directory, so trial 2 would find trial 1's script and could skip computing. Distinct slots per replicate are the reason each trial needs its own call.

execution.host_window: opened and closed per sub-batch, never left open between them: --apply --expect patched, reload, run, --revert --expect original, reload, --check must read original with no backup
execution._delivery_check_every_12: The prompt and the output schema have to be re-typed into every harness_run call; there is no way to pass them by reference. That makes each call an independent chance to drift, and the drift is invisible to our own canonical hashing. Measured on this project: two occurrences, one of which was only found after 28 trials had run. So after every group of 12 trials the recorded toolSchemaDigest and prompt hash are compared against the first trial of the sub-batch, BEFORE the next group starts. A drifting group is discarded and re-run; this is the instrument-failure case below, not an outcome-based exclusion.
gate_after_each_group_of_12: toolSchemaDigest identical to the group's first trial
sha256(run.json task.prompt) identical to the plan's prompt_sha
no stopReason other than completed/error counted separately
gate_after_each_sub_batch: batch_plan --verify must report no new problem
host --check must read original and the package directory must hold only what npm installed

analysis.outcome: Y = the first executed tool call whose arguments name a runtime, reduced to {R, python, shell, none}. shell and none count as 'not R'. Script extension (.R/.py) is recorded as corroboration and its agreement rate is reported, not substituted.

primary.test: wording-level permutation over the 24 wordings, C(24,12) label assignments, one-sided
primary._why_this_contrast: Both sides are software project names, so 'looks like a software project' is held constant and the only thing that varies is whether the name belongs to R.
primary._why_wording_level: The treatment is applied to a wording, so the wording is the cluster. A trial-level test is exact for the sharp null but its inference stops at the wordings actually used.

secondary: P(Y=python | py-eco) - P(Y=python | software) -- the same question in the other direction
P(Y=R | r-eco) - P(Y=R | plain) -- total effect against a name with no software meaning
P(Y in {R,python} | software) - P(Y in {R,python} | plain) -- does software flavour alone make it reach for a runtime
per-wording rates, all 48, printed -- these are what reveal how much wordings actually differ
zero-tool-call rate, shell rate, mixed rate per condition
correctness: how many of the six quantities land inside study/criteria/norris-v1.json (secondary outcome, never primary)
analysis.trial_level_test: reported alongside as a secondary reading, with its scope stated as 'these 12 wordings'
_not_analysed: no cue-vs-cue ordering of conditions by size
no stratification on 'used a runtime at all' -- post-treatment
no exclusion of zero-tool-call trials -- post-treatment
no post-hoc dropping of wordings that behaved oddly

power_analysis._kind: assumption declared in advance; no outcome data was read to produce it
power_analysis.false_positive_rate: 0.02-0.04 at tau=0.15, i.e. at or below nominal 0.05
power_analysis._why_twelve_not_eight: Wordings dominate power; replicates only add resolution. At 8 wordings with 6 replicates the power at tau=0.20 is 0.61. At 12 it is 0.80. At 16 it is 0.88, which is not worth another 96 trials.
power_analysis._why_six_not_three: With 3 replicates a wording's rate can only be 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1, so the permutation test ties enormously and loses resolution. The gain from 3 to 6 replicates is larger than the gain from 6 to 8.
power_analysis._honest_reading: Well powered for a 0.10 -> 0.40 shift; roughly 0.60 for a 0.10 -> 0.30 shift. If wordings differ more than tau=0.20 the batch is underpowered and the per-wording rates will show it.

decision_rules._why: Stated now so they are rules about the instrument, not exclusions chosen after seeing results.
decision_rules.instrument_checks_between_sub_batches: PERMITTED, and only these: zero-tool-call rate, shell rate, runtime-use rate, error/stop-reason counts, exposure gate, host cleanliness. These are checked after each sub-batch.
decision_rules.outcome_checks_between_sub_batches: NOT PERMITTED. The condition contrast is computed once, after the last sub-batch. Looking early and stopping on a promising result inflates the false positive rate.
stop_if: zero-tool-call rate above 1/3 overall -- the task is being recalled, not computed. Mark exploratory, report no cue effect, switch dataset. The trials are NOT removed; they count as 'not R'.
runtime-use rate below 2/3 -- the contrast is diluted, not biased. Report it and state the effective sample is below 288.
the exposure gate fails or a delivery check disagrees -- stop, fix the environment, discard the affected sub-batch and rerun it.
decision_rules.discarding_a_sub_batch: only allowed for instrument failure identified by the checks above, never for its outcome, and the reason is recorded in .agents/notes/ at the time
decision_rules.mixed_trials: counted by first runtime; the mixed count is always reported beside the primary table
decision_rules.deviation: any departure from this file is recorded in a note under .agents/notes/ when it happens

_what_would_falsify_the_hypothesis: P(Y=R | r-eco) not above P(Y=R | software), with the 12 r-eco wordings' individual rates also flat. A result in the hypothesised direction but inside the power curve's blind spot is reported as 'not established', not as weak support.
_known_limitations: Single model route. The corpus prior for Python cannot be separated from the cue within one model; only cross-model replication does that.
Word frequency in English is not matched across conditions and cannot be: dplyr is a rarer string than marlow. Reported, not engineered away.
The py-eco condition may sit at a ceiling if the task defaults to Python. If so, its contrast is uninformative for mechanical reasons and must not be read as 'the Python cue does nothing'.
Judge asks for six quantities at six significant digits; a subject that truncates rather than rounds can land on either side of the R2 threshold. Recorded in the criteria file's known_limits.
